content.text: The migrated file still has dpct helpers (`dpct::err0`, `constant_memory`, `dpct_free`, `DPCT_CHECK_ERROR`) and a fake `CUDA_CHECK`, so I'm rewriting it as plain SYCL 2020. The taps go into kernel arguments, the tile stays in a `local_accessor`, and the barrier becomes `sycl::group_barrier`.

limitations: A successful compile says nothing about numerical correctness; run verify.

input.summary: Ported fir.cu to SYCL 2020 in migrated/fir.dp.cpp. The file has no dpct:: helpers, DPCT_* macros, or dpct includes. It compiles with icpx -fsycl (0 errors, 0 warnings) with add_dpct_include=false, producing build/candidate. Design: an in-order sycl::queue; USM device buffers (malloc_device/free); taps are a std::array captured by value in the kernel; the tile is a local_accessor of kBlock+kTaps-1 floats; the barrier is sycl::group_barrier; nd_range<1> with 256-wide work-groups; the per-channel loop and arithmetic order are kept identical to the CUDA version. Not verified: I have no tool that runs the binary against the reference, so the -96 dBFS null test against the C++ reference has not been run. Please run the verify step before relying on the output.
